summary: @servicetitan/carto-charts-react ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: Package published as @servicetitan/carto-charts-react advertises itself as a thin React wrapper around echarts, and dist/index.js matches that description. However, package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs", and setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/... at install time and then invokes bunPath on a sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (header "// @bun @bun-cjs") wrapped in a string-array rotator + char-map decoder obfuscator (WV8StW rotator over the n7gIxM constant array, hc1jfK9 decoder). setup.mjs itself uses _0x-style renamed identifiers and stashes literal strings (URLs, spawn flags, /etc/os-release, Alpine) inside per-call wrapper objects. A React chart wrapper has no need to fetch a second language runtime at install and execute an obfuscated payload with it; the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern combined with heavy obfuscation of install-time-reachable code and a scope name resembling a SaaS vendor is consistent with a scope-hijack or malicious publish that achieves arbitrary code execution on any installer's machine during npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
